mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 0.5% signals monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a federal funds rate below 0.5%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2 percentage points over a month indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns in the subsequent 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following a 0.2pp increase in unemployment, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a 5% increase in housing starts, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strong supply-side activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a 1% increase in industrial production, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds CPI (CPIAUCSL) growth over a quarter, it indicates real economic growth, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows when GDP growth exceeds CPI growth, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 50,000 jobs in a month, but the unemployment rate (UNRATE) does not decrease, it may signal labor market inefficiency, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 and UNRATE does not decrease
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following such a labor market signal, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) during a recession signals a potential economic rebound, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >1% in 1 month during a recession
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a 1% increase in real retail sales during a recession, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 50,000 jobs in a month signals a robust labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows following a 50,000 job increase in payroll employment, the hypothesis is falsified.
